story.text: 전주역 개찰구를 나서자마자, 팔짱을 낀 채 무심하게 서 있는 낯익은 얼굴이 보였다.
story.reading: jeon-ju-yeok gae-chal-gu-reul na-seo-ja-ma-ja, pal-jjang-eul kkin chae mu-sim-ha-ge seo it-neun nach-ik-eun eol-gul-i bo-yeot-da.
story.en: The moment I stepped out through the ticket gate at Jeonju Station, I spotted a familiar face standing there with arms crossed, looking indifferent.

story.text: "오랜만이다." 하늘이 짧게 한마디 던지고는, 내 캐리어부터 빼앗듯 가져갔다.
story.reading: o-raen-man-i-da. ha-neul-i jjalb-ge han-ma-di deon-ji-go-neun, nae kae-ri-eo-bu-teo ppae-at-deut ga-jyeo-gat-da.
story.en: "Long time no see." Haneul tossed out one short line, then practically snatched my suitcase away.

story.text: "야, 그래도 반갑다는 말 정도는 해줘야지." 내가 투덜대자, 그는 픽 웃었다. "지금 이게 내 나름의 반가운 표정이야."
story.reading: ya, geu-rae-do ban-gap-da-neun mal jeong-do-neun hae-jwo-ya-ji. nae-ga tu-deol-dae-ja, geu-neun pik us-eot-da. ji-geum i-ge nae na-reum-ui ban-ga-un pyo-jeong-i-ya.
story.en: "Hey, you could at least say you're glad to see me." I grumbled, and he smirked. "This, right here, is my version of glad."

story.text: "그래도 역까지 마중 나와줬잖아. 그거면 됐지." 그가 능청스럽게 덧붙였다.
story.reading: geu-rae-do yeok-kka-ji ma-jung na-wa-jwot-jan-a. geu-geo-myeon dwaet-ji. geu-ga neung-cheong-seu-reop-ge deot-but-yeot-da.
story.en: "But I still came out to meet you at the station. That should be enough." he added, playing it cool.

story.text: 개찰구를 나서며 그가 내 얼굴을 슬쩍 훑어봤다. "얼굴 왜 이렇게 상했어. 잠은 좀 잤어?" 정곡을 찌르는 그 한마디에 나는 말문이 막혔다.
story.reading: gae-chal-gu-reul na-seo-myeo geu-ga nae eol-gul-eul seul-jjeok hult-eo-bwat-da. eol-gul wae i-reo-ke sang-haet-eo. jam-eun jom jat-eo? jeong-gog-eul jji-reu-neun geu han-ma-di-e na-neun mal-mun-i mak-hyeot-da.
story.en: As we walked out, he glanced over my face. "Why do you look so worn out? Did you even sleep?" That one line hit the nail right on the head, and I couldn't find words.

story.text: "너는 여전하네. 남 얼굴부터 걱정하는 거." 내가 웃으며 말하자, 그는 대답 없이 성큼성큼 앞서 걸었다.
story.reading: neo-neun yeo-jeon-ha-ne. nam eol-gul-bu-teo geok-jeong-ha-neun geo. nae-ga us-eu-myeo mal-ha-ja, geu-neun dae-dap eop-si seong-keum-seong-keum ap-seo geol-eot-da.
story.en: "You haven't changed. Always worrying about someone else's face first." I said with a laugh, and he walked on ahead without answering.

story.text: 역 광장에 붙은 "전주" 표지판을 보니, 그제야 이 여행이 진짜 시작됐다는 게 실감 났다. 오랜 친구와 함께라서 더 든든했다.
story.reading: yeok gwang-jang-e but-eun jeon-ju pyo-ji-pan-eul bo-ni, geu-je-ya i yeo-haeng-i jin-jja si-jak-dwaet-da-neun ge sil-gam nat-da. o-raen chin-gu-wa ham-kke-ra-seo deo deun-deun-haet-da.
story.en: Seeing the "Jeonju" sign at the station plaza, it finally hit me that this trip had really begun. Having an old friend along made it feel even more reassuring.

words.example_en: Long time no see, how have you been?

words.meaning: to come out to meet/greet someone
words.example_en: My friend came out to meet me at the airport.

words.meaning: to be glad, happy (to see someone)
words.example_en: I'm really glad to see you again.

words.meaning: to be the same as before, unchanged
words.example_en: You haven't changed a bit, still the same as ever.

words.meaning: to hit the nail on the head, hit a sore spot
words.example: 그의 말이 정곡을 찔러서 아무 말도 못 했다.
words.example_reading: geu-ui mal-i jeong-gog-eul jjil-leo-seo a-mu mal-do mot haet-da
words.example_en: His words hit the nail right on the head, so I couldn't say anything.

sentences.en: Long time no see, how have you been?
My friend came out to meet me at the station.
I'm really glad to see you again.
You haven't changed a bit, still the same as ever.
His words hit the nail right on the head.
